detail: The adapter cost table said 'Node only', and the gap was stated honestly rather than measured: 'the adapters share a design but not an implementation, so the Node number does not transfer to Go or Python'. This measures both, by the same method as adapter-benchmark.mjs so the numbers are comparable: a real server over a real socket with keep-alive on, four shapes per round (unmounted baseline, mounted but untraced, mounted and traced, and a SECOND baseline), alternating rounds, medians, and the gap between the two baselines reported as the method's own noise floor so a number smaller than the noise cannot be read as signal. Go lives in its own module under validation/backend/adapter-benchmark-go with a replace directive onto this checkout, so it always measures this tree; Python drives a bare ASGI app under uvicorn rather than FastAPI, because a router's per-request work is identical in all four shapes but large enough to shrink the delta the benchmark exists to show. Both run in the sdk-backend-reference job, which already has Go and uv. Measured on an Apple M1 Ultra at the CI defaults (3000 runs, 5 rounds): Go baseline 53-70us with a traced cost of 24-28us and an untraced cost below the noise floor, which puts it alongside Node; Python baseline 179-237us with a traced cost of 42-77us and an untraced cost of -21 to +6.5us, single digits at most and of unresolvable sign. Ceilings are sized for a shared runner rather than this laptop, and Python's are wider than the other two because the interpreter's own run-to-run variance is wider. docs/backend-sdk.md now carries a three-row table with the spread stated, and the remaining unmeasured set is named exactly (the per-dependency capture path, plus the Rust, Java, .NET, PHP and Ruby adapters) instead of the blanket 'every language other than Node'.
